meta.title: Myth: you need to feel sore to grow

sources.label: Schoenfeld & Contreras, 2013
sources.citation: Schoenfeld BJ, Contreras B. Is postexercise muscle soreness a valid indicator of muscular adaptations? Strength Cond J. 2013;35(5):16-21.

sources.label: Damas et al., 2016 · schematic
sources.citation: Damas F, et al. Resistance training-induced changes in integrated myofibrillar protein synthesis are related to hypertrophy only after attenuation of muscle damage. J Physiol. 2016;594(18):5209-5222.

scenes.narration: No soreness after training means no gains, right?
Wrong. Soreness is just tiny damage from a move your muscle isn't used to. It's not a growth signal.
In one study, soreness dropped fast, but real growth only kicked in after week three.
